Generation prompt

Create a single finished portrait-oriented editorial art poster with a strict two-panel vertical split, upper and lower halves equal in height (50% / 50%), clean horizontal division at the exact midpoint, overall aspect ratio approximately 4:5.

UPPER HALF — original realistic photograph:
A quiet small cream-colored mixed-breed dog sitting calmly in a soft sunlit corner beside a window, 3/4 view facing slightly right, floppy ears, dark gentle eyes, black nose, paws visible, clear centered subject and unmistakable silhouette. Warm morning light, pale mint rug, a little blurred greenery outside the window, soft cream wall, airy bright healing atmosphere, shallow depth of field, true natural photography, subtle film grain. The dog is the only visual anchor; the room is only a quiet supporting backdrop. No people, no architecture as subject, no clutter.

LOWER HALF — faithful woodcut reinterpretation of the exact same dog:
Reconstruct the same dog, same 3/4 seated pose, same ear shape, head angle, proportions, direction, and quiet narrative relationship, as a floating limited-color handmade woodcut / linocut print impression on warm ivory paper. Do not copy the photograph background and do not apply a photo filter. Simplify aggressively into a few readable shapes: dog silhouette, paws, window-light direction, and a small hint of the mint rug. Use a single visual anchor with large warm paper negative space. Hand-carved awkward marks: uneven knife-cut lines, hesitant contours, blunt turns, broken edges, missing ink, dry-brush skips, misregistration, rough grain, paper showing through, imperfect worn edges that dissolve naturally. No complete rectangular frame. The mark should feel pressed onto paper and fade at the perimeter.

COLOR + TYPE:
Palette derived from the photo but fresh and light: ivory and cream paper, pale blush pink, misty sage/mint green, soft sky blue, butter yellow, light apricot/coral, pale ochre, and a restrained charcoal ink. Matte layered ink, low-to-medium saturation, high brightness, soft contrast, gentle and restorative, never dark, muddy, heavy, or overly retro. Integrate restrained archival/typewriter typography into the lower print: exact readable title “QUIET PAWS” in small uppercase, placed along the lower edge of the print or following the dog’s visual axis; tiny secondary notes “WINDOW / STILL / WARM” in a subtle monospaced serif/typewriter style. Text is part of the composition, not an explanation. Avoid any other words, logos, borders, stickers, or decorative templates.

Art direction:
The top and bottom must visibly echo each other while remaining two distinct media: real photography above, hand-pulled imperfect woodcut below. Quiet, warm, clean, nostalgic without gloom, sophisticated contemporary printmaking, generous whitespace, no cartoon style, no smooth vector outlines, no generic travel poster, no full background replication, no extra animals, no distorted anatomy. Ensure the lower dog is clearly the same individual as the upper dog at a glance.
